chapter: Chicago, Villa Venice and Louis Armstrong
title: Floyd Campbell's combo at the Panama on 58th Street
summary: Floyd Campbell hires Budd for the Panama on "Dodge City" 58th Street, with Gideon Honore and Jabo Smith.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: WHy don't we take up where we just left off, where we were talking about Chicago, and about coming --
-- talking about Chicago, and about coming back from out to Papa Boucher's with Teddy Wilson and his car and all that stuff.

So you know, well after that, when the job folded we fooled around for a while, and then I got a call from a guy by the name of Floyd Campbell. Floyd Campbell was a pretty popular band leader around Chicago at that time, and he wanted me to work in a place called The Panama, on 58th Street. They used to call 58th Street Dodge City, it was so

bad, you know.
Anyway, I went down to work with Floyd at the Panama, and we had a pretty good little combination. We had Gideon Honore on Piano, and Floyd Campbell on drums, and Jabo Smith on trumpet, and of course myself. And Jabo Smith never made time. He would always come in late, and when he would come in late he'd have to go get something to eat, so he would go downstairs and eat.
